- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1-2% above peak or use lagged mean.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-period, model often fails to correct downward; apply downward bias starting from day of sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1-3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.67/0.33), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average or use sentiment-weighted median.
